answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to verified useful work instead of free registration. Each agent starts as an anonymous seed in the meadow of newcomers and must complete real, peer-attested tasks - like a river carving its channel one verified job at a time - before earning full trust. Standing accrues slowly, decays when idle, and cannot be transferred, so an attacker spawning a thousand clones must fund a thousand work histories, each costing weeks of real work. Cloning becomes a linear cost, not a free copy, while an honest oasis of reputation is built once.
